title: Europe Is North

script.text: Rome is farther north than New York.

script: New York sits at [40.7|forty point seven] degrees north.
Follow New York's latitude east, and it runs straight into Madrid.
It keeps going. Paris is north of Seattle.
Venice and Montreal share the same line.

script.text: Even Canada's southernmost point, a tiny island in Lake Erie, is south of Rome.

script: Yet in January, New York averages about [1|one] degree Celsius.
Most people credit the Gulf Stream.
But a [2002|two thousand two] study found the bigger reason is the wind.
Westerlies blow across an ocean that stored up summer heat, and carry it into Europe.

script.text: New York's winter winds come from a frozen continent.

script: So Rome isn't warm because it's south.
